jagtap2025: Jagtap, Shinde, Marade, Sawant, Sable, Mahalle (2025). A Comprehensive Dataset of Tomato Plant Diseases for National Predictive Analytics and Crop Health Management. Mendeley Data. DOI:10.17632/ztncd79yhk.1
general: General agricultural extension guidance (TNAU / standard plant-pathology practice). Verify locally with your agricultural officer or KVK.
spray_wind: Agriculture Victoria / GRDC spray-drift guidance: ideal wind ~3-15 km/h, do not spray at 20 km/h or more. https://agriculture.vic.gov.au/farm-management/chemicals/spraying-agricultural-chemicals/managing-spray-drift/a-guide-to-estimating-wind-speed
rainfast: Fungicide rainfastness: protectants such as mancozeb need ~1.5-2 h drying (labels up to 6 h) and are partly washed off by >5 mm rain. https://ext.grapepathology.org/rains-and-fungicide-sprays
sulfur_heat: Sulfur phytotoxicity risk above 32°C (AWRI Agrochemical update, Oct 2021; US product labels: do not apply above 90°F). https://www.awri.com.au/information_services/ebulletin/2021/10/13/agrochemical-update-october-2021-using-sulfur-to-protect-vines-particularly-under-cool-conditions/
hutton: Hutton Criteria for late blight: two consecutive days with minimum temperature ≥10°C and ≥6 h of relative humidity ≥90% (AHDB, 2017; Smith Period uses ≥11 h). https://potatoes.ahdb.org.uk/development-and-implementation-of-a-new-national-warning-system-for-potato-late-blight-in-great-britain-hutton-criteria
tomcast: TOM-CAST daily disease severity values from leaf-wetness hours and temperature (Madden et al. 1978; table from Proc. 2015 Wisconsin Crop Management Conference). https://extension.soils.wisc.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/68/2015/06/Frost-2015-WCMC-Proceedings.pdf
frac_irac: FRAC (fungicide) and IRAC (insecticide) mode-of-action classification - rotate groups to delay resistance. https://www.frac.info / https://irac-online.org
shc: Soil Health Card scheme, Govt. of India (Dept. of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare): soil-parameter rating classes (pH, EC, organic carbon, available N, P, K, S, B, Mn) used on the card; Low/Medium/High classes after Muhr et al. (1965). https://soilhealth.dac.gov.in
dtpa: Lindsay, W.L. & Norvell, W.A. (1978). Development of a DTPA soil test for zinc, iron, manganese and copper. Soil Sci. Soc. Am. J. 42:421-428 (critical limits Zn 0.6, Fe 4.5, Cu 0.2 ppm).
tnau_tomato: TNAU Agritech Portal / Crop Production Guide (Horticulture), Tomato: FYM 25 t/ha; varieties 150:100:50 kg N:P2O5:K2O per ha (N half basal, half top-dressed at 30 days); hybrids 200:250:250. Soil-test adjustment Low +25 %, Medium 100 %, High -25 %. https://agritech.tnau.ac.in
jones_woltz: Jones, J.P. & Woltz, S.S. (1981). Fusarium-incited diseases of tomato and potato and their control. In: Fusarium: Diseases, Biology and Taxonomy, pp. 157-168 - liming to pH 6.5-7.0 and nitrate-N suppress Fusarium wilt.
ber_calcium: Blossom-end rot is a calcium-transport disorder made worse by low soil Ca, salinity and irregular watering (e.g. Ho & White 2005, Ann. Bot. 95:571-581; Saure 2001, Sci. Hortic. 90:193-208).
phi: Pre-harvest interval (days from the last spray to picking): conservative default values chosen for decision support, set at or above typical tomato label intervals for each product type (India CIB&RC registrations, US EPA labels). Intervals differ between brands and formulations — the label on the pack is final. Botanicals: wash fruit before sale.
